title: Affine annihilator ideals commute with restriction to basic opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$ and $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, put $D_U(f)=X_f\subseteq U$, the affine basic open [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme]. If $\rho:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(D_U(f))$ is restriction, then $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X(D_U(f))}F(D_U(f))=\rho(\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}F(U))\mathcal O_X(D_U(f))$. Here $\operatorname{Ann}_R M=\{r\in R:rm=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$.

source.place: Lemma 05JU (morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-support), final paragraph; the finite localization annihilator identity is the localization specialization of Algebra Lemma 07T8 (algebra-lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change).

proof.text: First prove restriction preserves finite type on an arbitrary site with binary products and pullbacks, a sheaf of rings, and sheafification and local-bijectivity on every slice and iterated slice site. Specialize this general theorem to the scheme open site to restrict a finite local generating cover of F to U. The iterated slice-site pushforward functors preserve colimits and the unit, so their images of the finite generating families still generate. Thus F.over U is finite type. Apply the affine finite-type criterion to obtain Module.Finite O_X(U) F(U). The basic-open ring restriction is a localization at f.

The canonical affine section base-change map is bijective. Swap its tensor factors and use its stated linearity for the basic-open ring to make it a linear equivalence O_X(D(f)) tensor_O_X(U) F(U) -> F(D(f)). On 1 tensor m it is restriction of m, by the stated pure-tensor formula. Mathlib IsBaseChange.of_equiv and isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange therefore give IsLocalizedModule (powers f) for restriction.

For a finite module M over R, any localization ring A and module localization g:M->N, show map(Ann_R M)=Ann_A N directly. Forward: for a in Ann_R M and y in N take a denominator s with s*y=g(m). Then s*(a*y)=g(a*m)=0; denominator multiplication is injective, so a*y=0. Reverse: for z in Ann_A N write z*image(s)=image(r). It follows that g(r*m)=0 for every m. Choose finite generators e_j of M. The localization zero criterion supplies c_j with c_j*(r*e_j)=0. The product t of all c_j kills r*e_j for all j, and hence r*M, because the generators span M. Thus tr is in Ann_R M and z*image(ts)=image(tr), proving membership in the extended ideal by Mathlib IsLocalization.mem_map_algebraMap_iff. This includes no generators (t=1), zero ring, and localization at zero. Apply this algebra argument to the localization of step 2.
